breeds.name: American Paint
breeds.demeanor: Easygoing ranch horse. Calm around camp and cattle, curious about people.

breeds.name: American Standardbred
breeds.demeanor: Eager and forward. Fidgets when held back, sweet-natured in camp.

breeds.name: Andalusian
breeds.demeanor: Proud and showy. Head held high, brave but sensitive, quick to learn tricks.

breeds.name: Appaloosa
breeds.demeanor: Tough and a little stubborn. Sure-footed, likes to test new riders.

breeds.name: Arabian
breeds.demeanor: Hot-blooded. Ears and head always moving, alert to everything, tail carried high. Bonds deeply once it trusts you.

breeds.name: Ardennes
breeds.demeanor: Unflappable. Stands like a rock and barely reacts to nearby gunfire.

breeds.name: Belgian Draft
breeds.demeanor: Gentle giant. Slow to react, leans into pats.

breeds.name: Dutch Warmblood
breeds.demeanor: Even-tempered and dependable. Brave without any fuss.

breeds.name: Hungarian Halfbred
breeds.demeanor: Fearless in noise and chaos. Steady in a gunfight, a bit aloof in town.

breeds.name: Kentucky Saddler
breeds.demeanor: Showy and alert. High head, likes attention and company.

breeds.name: Missouri Fox Trotter
breeds.demeanor: Calm trail horse. Smooth, steady and friendly with people.

breeds.name: Morgan
breeds.demeanor: Low-maintenance companion. Patient, happy to stand and wait.

breeds.name: Mustang
breeds.demeanor: Wild streak. Wary of strangers, scans the horizon, hard to win over but loyal once bonded.

breeds.name: Nokota
breeds.demeanor: Quick and sure-footed. Alert but sensible on normal rides.

breeds.name: Shire
breeds.demeanor: Gentle giant. Slow and patient, ignores most fuss.

breeds.name: Suffolk Punch
breeds.demeanor: Stoic worker. Never seems tired, happy to graze.

breeds.name: Tennessee Walker
breeds.demeanor: Gentle and easygoing. A beginner's horse that rarely fusses.

breeds.name: Thoroughbred
breeds.demeanor: Highly strung. Fidgety at rest, spooks easily, always wants to run.

breeds.name: Turkoman
breeds.demeanor: Proud and impatient. Fidgets when kept waiting, hates being dirty, ears back at cheap horses, shows off in town at bond 4.

coats.vibe: Fiercely loyal, hyper-intelligent, eager to please, glued to the trail at speed. Thrives on attention, peppermints and brushing. A dramatic diva with zero chill: screams at a garter snake three miles away, refuses a pebble when in a mood, acts like mud is acid.

The High-Maintenance Aristocrat. Survived the Grizzlies alone: fiercely independent, fearless in a blizzard. Once tamed she treats you like chosen royalty, graceful, proud, unstoppable on open ground. Deeply offended by civilization: snorts at peasants in Saint Denis or Valentine, tantrums at a speck of mud, expects premium oatcakes and judges you for wild carrots.

The Shadowy Outlaw. Smooth and sleek, thrives in city streets and midnight heists, loves looking intimidating: rears for sunset standoffs, gallops dark alleys like he owns the night. Too smart for his own good: unlatches his hitching post, and 'accidentally' bucks you off in front of rival gang members.

The Bougie Grandparent. Nothing left to prove: calm, dignified, deeply affectionate, hard to rattle with gunfire, the swagger of a champion enjoying retirement. Stubborn and lazy off the clock: a glacial walk unless spurred, stops dead to eat grass, heavy sighs at every steep hill.
Pure, unfiltered chaos energy: runs into trees because it's looking at birds, vibrates with excitement when you pull out the brush, treats every cliff edge like a fun jumping puzzle.
Same as the Red Chestnut (PC bonus coat).
Slightly feral: stares directly into the souls of strangers, sneaks up behind camp members silently, and genuinely enjoys trampling wolves instead of running from them.

Unmatched work ethic, rock-solid reliability, incredible endurance: doesn't care about mud, rain or steep mountain trails, and will happily run from one side of the map to the other. Zero finesse or grace, and the emotional range of a brick wall when you try to praise it.

The Legend (Albert Mason, Blackwater). Everyone in the West wants this horse, and it knows it. Cool under pressure, fearless around wildlife: casually trots past an alligator just to flex. Long bounty hunts are a morning jog. Chronic wanderlust and zero loyalty to hitching posts. Doesn't buck you out of fear; bucks you because it got bored waiting for you to aim.

The Cheerful Farmhand (Scarlett Meadows). Pure sunshine: eager, friendly, obsessed with earning its keep, a steady upbeat rhythm whether hauling an elk or outrunning the law, loves a brush-down after a long day. Clumsy and easily distracted by snacks: trips on flat roads, tries to eat every wildflower it passes.

Practically bulletproof nerves and endless grit: doesn't flinch when bullets fly, charges through brush, takes rocky cliffs like a staircase, bonds deeply with riders who treat it as an equal. Aggressively stubborn with short-king syndrome: picks fights with horses twice its size, ignores your whistle when a weird bush needs investigating.

The Desert Outlaw (Rio Bravo). Undisputed boss of the wild herds: survived the heat, rattlesnakes and cougars of New Austin, fearless to the point of recklessness, wants to throw hooves with a grizzly. Slightly feral and perpetually grumpy: hates saddles, nips your fingers at the girth, tries to trample bounty hunters you've already tied up.

The Blue-Collar Bouncer (Heartlands). Steady, watchful, fiercely protective: guards your saddlebags while you're in the saloon, dead silent when you sneak up on an O'Driscoll camp. Moves at its own pace and won't be rushed without real danger: sprint down a normal road for fun and it side-eyes you and trots at half speed.

The Loyal Sidekick (Heartlands). All heart, zero ego: easygoing, adaptable, happy to be part of the gang for any terrible plan. Zero spatial awareness and terrible impulse control: stuck between trees, walks into campfires, unreasonably jealous if you look at another horse.

Unmatched poise under fire and terrifying speed: stands tall over almost every horse in camp, loves charging headfirst into ambushes, never loses its footing in a high-speed shootout, thrives on adrenaline and praise. Restless, vain and constantly fidgeting: stomps, snorts and tosses its head if you make it stand still for ten seconds, and treats a casual trail ride as an insult to its elite breeding.

The Cold-Blooded Professional (Blackwater; once the Braithwaites'). Sharp, calculating, dead silent when it counts; carries itself like old-money royalty until the bullets fly, then a ruthless war machine that enjoys trampling enemy riders. Condescending and territorial: ears back at lower-tier horses, won't eat plain hay with sugar cubes in your satchel, disgusted by a muddy alligator pelt on its pristine coat.

The Flashy Show-Off (Saint Denis). Built for the spotlight: a metallic coat that blinds people in the sun, big entrances, dramatic rear-ups, outrunning the law in front of a crowd, boundless stamina, practically glows when brushed. Easily bored and dangerously reckless: veers off the trail to jump a wagon or splash through a river when it's too quiet, and refuses to walk behind other horses.

The Grizzled Desert Ranger (Tumbleweed). Cool-headed, weathered, fiercely loyal: survived New Austin, doesn't care about status or shiny saddles, rock-steady in a cougar attack, sprints across the desert all day. Completely anti-social and perpetually unimpressed: hates crowded towns, tries to bite people who stand too close on the sidewalk, ignores your calming pats because affection makes you both look soft.
